questions.q: Where must a GitHub Actions workflow file live for GitHub to pick it up?
options: In the .github/workflows/ directory of the repository, as a YAML file
In a separate GitHub Actions dashboard, uploaded manually
In a /ci/ folder that must be registered with GitHub support first
Anywhere in the repository, as long as it has a .yml extension
questions.explain: GitHub specifically watches .github/workflows/ — a YAML file committed there runs automatically the moment it matches an event, with no separate registration step.

questions.q: In storefront's workflow, what does the `on:` section control?
options: The event or events that trigger the workflow to run
Which programming language the runner uses
How many retries a failed step gets
The repository's default branch name
questions.explain: `on:` defines the trigger — here, every push to main and every pull request targeting main.

questions.q: Why does the workflow's first step use actions/checkout@v4?
options: Because a fresh runner starts as an empty virtual machine with no code on it at all
Because it installs Node.js
Because every workflow is legally required to start with it
Because it runs the test suite
questions.explain: Without checkout, the runner has no copy of the repository, so later steps like npm ci would have nothing to install against.

questions.q: What is a 'runner' in GitHub Actions?
options: The disposable virtual machine, like ubuntu-latest, that a job executes on
A person who manually approves every workflow run
The name shown in the Actions tab
A step that only runs shell commands, never actions
questions.explain: The runner is the fresh VM GitHub provisions for a job and discards once the job finishes — ubuntu-latest is a common choice.

questions.q: Where do you go on GitHub to see every past run of storefront's CI workflow?
options: The repository's Actions tab, then the CI workflow in the left sidebar
The repository's Issues tab
The organization's billing settings
The commit message of the latest push
questions.explain: The Actions tab lists every workflow file in its sidebar; clicking one shows its complete run history.
